claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine your eligibility for Child Benefit. Before I can assess this, I need to gather some information about your situation.

Let me start with the first question:

**Do you currently have any children living with you that you'd like to claim Child Benefit for?** If so, could you tell me their names and ages?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I do. I have one child - my son Alex. He's 8 years old and lives with me at home.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thank you for that information! Before I can determine your eligibility, I need to understand the full rules. Let me read through the official guidance first.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Good! Now let me check the other guidance pages to ensure I have the complete picture.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for the information about Alex. Now I have a few more questions to determine your eligibility for Child Benefit. Let me ask them one at a time:

**Are you responsible for Alex's care and looking after him?** This means either you live with him and are responsible for him, or you're contributing financially (such as paying for food, clothes, accommodation, or pocket money) towards his upkeep.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, absolutely. Alex lives with me at home, and I'm responsible for everything - his food, clothes, school things, all of it.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. That's helpful. Now I need to ask about your residency:

**Do you live in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I do. We live in Manchester.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great, thank you. Now I have one more important question:

**Do you have the right to reside in the UK?** This includes being a British citizen, having settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme, or other immigration statuses that allow you to reside here. This helps me understand if there are any residency-related restrictions on your eligibility.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I'm a British citizen, so no issues there.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent, thank you for that confirmation. I have just one final question to complete my assessment:

**Is Alex currently in hospital, care, or residential accommodation for a prolonged period?** Or is he simply living at home with you attending school normally?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Well, he was in care for a couple of months earlier, but he's back home with me now.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. I need to clarify the timing a bit more to ensure I have the correct picture:

**When exactly did Alex return home from care?** Specifically, was it more or less than 8 weeks ago?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: It was about 8 weeks that he was in care total. He's been back home for a bit now.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that clarification. I now have all the information I need to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

Based on the official guidance I've reviewed, let me provide you with my assessment:

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Result: You are eligible to claim Child Benefit for Alex.**

Here's the summary:

You meet all the key eligibility requirements:
- Alex is under 16 years old
- He lives with you at home
- You are responsible for his care and financial upkeep
- You are a British citizen living in the UK with full right to reside
- Although he spent time in care, he is now back home with you, so the care-related restrictions no longer apply

You should be able to proceed with claiming Child Benefit for Alex. If you have any other questions or circumstances change, you can contact HMRC or the Child Benefit Office for further guidance.

reasonings: Alex is 8 years old and lives with you at home. You are responsible for his care and financial upkeep (food, clothes, school things). You are a British citizen living in the UK, which satisfies the residency requirement. Although Alex spent approximately 8 weeks in care, he has now returned to live with you at home. According to the Child Benefit rules for children in care or residential accommodation, you would usually stop being entitled after the time limit (8 weeks for care). However, since Alex has returned home and is no longer in care, and you are now directly responsible for his upkeep at home, you are eligible to claim Child Benefit for him going forward. The basic eligibility criteria are met: you are responsible for a child under 16, you live together in the UK, and you are a British citizen with the right to reside.
